questions.q: Who were the sons of Aaron?
questions.a: The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

questions.q: What happened to Nadab and Abihu?
questions.a: They died before their father died and had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar became priests instead.

questions.q: Who helped David divide the priests into their service groups?
questions.a: Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Ithamar, helped him.

questions.q: How many leaders came from Eleazar’s descendants, and how many came from Ithamar’s descendants?
questions.a: Sixteen leaders came from Eleazar’s descendants and eight came from Ithamar’s descendants.

questions.q: How did they divide the priests for their service in the sanctuary?
questions.a: They divided them by casting lots.

questions.q: Who wrote down the names of the priests as they were assigned to their divisions?
questions.a: Shemaiah, the son of Nethanel, a Levite scribe, wrote them down while the king, the officials, and the priests watched.

questions.q: What determined the order in which the twenty-four divisions of priests would serve?
questions.a: The order was determined by casting lots, from Jehoiarib’s division, which was first, to Maaziah’s division, which was twenty-fourth.

questions.q: What instructions did Aaron give to his descendants for their service?
questions.a: Aaron instructed them, as Yahweh had commanded him, in the duties of the priestly service.

questions.q: What do all the men named have in common?
questions.a: The men in these verses are all descendants of Levi and leaders of their clans.

questions.q: What did the Levites also do, just as the priests, the descendants of Aaron, had done?
questions.a: They also cast lots in the presence of King David and the other leaders.

commentary.text: The divisions of the priests and Levites.

—When every one has, knows, and keeps his place and work, the more there are the better. In the mystical body of Christ, every member has its use, for the good of the whole. Christ is High Priest over the house of God, to whom all believers, being made priests, are to be in subjection. In Christ, no difference is made between bond and free, elder and younger. The younger brethren, if faithful and sincere, shall be no less acceptable to Christ than the fathers. May we all be children of the Lord, fitted to sing his praises for ever in his temple above.
